messages:

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: End of Quarter: cross-team score reconciliation & narrative edits

Team —

Attached is Q2_score_grid_v3.xlsx with the initial reconciliation across product, infra, and growth. I pulled together the raw inputs from each lead and applied the scoring rubric from the Q2 playbook (weights in tab "rubric_v2"). Two things for immediate attention:

1) Latency OKR (SLO99 @ 100ms): infra and product disagree on the severity adjustment. Product argues user-facing regressions justify a -2 delta; infra's telemetry shows 98.7% meeting target and requests -1.
2) Unit cost (inference $/1000 tokens) — growth scored this lower because of granularity differences in batch measurement; I marked as "needs reconciliation".

Ask: can we please resolve both items so I can lock scores and draft the QBR one-pager? Practical asks:
- Vivek: propose tie-break compromise for latency (and confirm you saw the telemetry excerpt I pasted into the doc).
- Laura: if you can pull one quick customer quote to illustrate the user impact, I’ll insert into the narrative.
- Marcus: can you take the lead on the final one-line narrative for the exec slide (90 seconds)?

Timeline: I want finalized scores by EOD Friday so I can ship the slide to Execs Saturday AM.

Attachments: Q2_score_grid_v3.xlsx (score sheet), customer-impact-examples.pdf (raw quotes)

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov | Head of GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: End of Quarter: cross-team score reconciliation & narrative edits

Olga — thanks for pulling this together. Quick read-through notes and a proposed compromise:

- Latency OKR: agree the rubric is ambiguous on severity adjustments for transient regressions vs sustained regressions. My recommendation: average the two proposed deltas and apply a +0 weight adjustment to the product-impact column to reflect front-door customer impact. That results in a net -1.5 (rounded down to -1 for the public score, and we capture a note in the appendix explaining the rationale).
- Unit cost: growth and infra are measuring at different percentiles. I asked the infra lead to recompute using growth's batching window (attached short CSV in the doc). That moves the cost metric up ~4% and changes the score from 6 -> 7.

I pasted the telemetry snippet at the top of the shared doc (see link). If everyone is okay with the approach above I can update the score sheet and add the short rationale for the appendix.

Simon from Acme Analytics also sent a short note about perceived latency in their integration (copied here). That supports keeping the user-impact weight slightly higher.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | SVP Product & Ops
Redwood Inference

Team — thanks all for the fast turnaround. I've consolidated the sheet per Vivek's approach and Laura's customer quote. Key outputs below and next steps for QBR slide pack: 

Final reconciled scores (high level):
- Latency (SLO99 @ 100ms): 7/10 (final adjustment -1; appendix note recorded)
- Unit cost (inference $/1000 tokens): 7/10 (growth/infra recomputed on common window)
- Reliability (incidents/M): 9/10
- Developer DX (time-to-deploy): 8/10

Draft 90-second narrative (please edit inline in the doc):
"Redwood ended Q2 with continued high reliability and meaningful improvements in developer velocity while contending with workload-driven latency pressure late in the quarter. We reconciled instrumentation and batching methodologies across infra and growth, which reduced apparent unit-cost variance and clarified tradeoffs. For latency, we applied a conservative adjustment but captured the customer impact and remediation plan in the appendix. Our roadmap for Q3 prioritizes targeted model kernel optimizations and expanded caching to regain headroom without compromising inference economics."

Action items (owners):
- Olga: finalize slide deck and send to Execs by Sun 10:00 AM PT.
- Vivek: paste the telemetry excerpt and short rationale into appendix (done).
- Laura: add the customer quote into the slide note (done).
- Marcus: produce 1-slide summary + 3 backup bullets for SRE and Product.

Attachments: consolidated slide request (I uploaded the slide stub into the shared doc)

If there are no objections by Sunday 9:00 AM PT I will publish this as the QBR narrative.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin | Director, Strategy & Analytics
